title: Burning and Suppression of Solids

sources.title: Thickness and Fuel Preheating Effects on Material Flammability in Microgravity from the BASS Experiment
Opposed-Flow Flame Spread in a Narrow Channel Apparatus over Thin PMMA Sheets

key_findings: Materials burn as well if not better than in normal gravity
fields.earth_applications: BASS results provide essential guidance to ground-based microgravity combustion research efforts.

conditions.label: Concurrent-flow air
evidence: Airflow speeds reaching as high as 40 cm/s

conditions.label: Opposed-flow air
evidence: Airflow speeds reaching as high as 40 cm/s

conditions.label: PMMA sphere, 17% oxygen, 12 cm/s flow
evidence: Flame sequence of a burning 2-cm diameter PMMA sphere at 17% oxygen and 12 cm/s flow.

conditions.label: PMMA sphere, 17% oxygen, less than 1 cm/s flow
evidence: Flame sequence of a burning PMMA sphere (1-cm diameter) at 17% oxygen and less than 1 cm/s.

conditions.label: PMMA rod, low-oxygen blowoff tests
evidence: Similar to the work done on cellulose in [8], this article explores the effect gap height has on the flame spread rate for 75 µm PMMA at 1 atm pressure and 21% oxygen concentration by volume in the SDSU NCA. Gap height tests were conducted with an opposed oxidizer velocity ranging from 7 to 35 cm/s. 2.

conditions.label: PMMA sheet, microgravity simulation
evidence: This article presents results from the SDSU NCA for clear, extruded polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) at 1 atm pressure, opposed oxidizer velocity ranging from 3 to 35 cm/s, oxygen concentration by volume at 21%, 30 %, and 50%, and fuel thicknesses of 50 and 75 µm.

paper_findings.text: Flame spread rate was fastest at an intermediate value of flow speed in opposed flow.
Flame spread rate increased linearly with increasing flow in concurrent flow.
Quenching extinction was observed around 1 cm/s in concurrent flow.

Flame spread rate for 75 µm PMMA at 1 atm pressure, 10 mm gap height, 7 cm/s opposed oxidizer velocity, and 21 percent oxygen concentration is 0.216 cm/s with an R-squared correlation coefficient of 0.9995.
NCA successfully simulates microgravity for thin PMMA sheets as well as thin cellulose fuels at 1 atm pressure.
Oxygen concentration plays a large role in the flame spread rate.
